ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 3
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. going
   C. goes
   D. went

3. When practising Attentive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Attentive Listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Attentive Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive Listening.

4. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.

5. When practising Guided Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Guided Writing.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Guided Writing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Guided Writing.

6. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

7. When practising Punctuation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Punctuation.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Punctuation.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Punctuation.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Punctuation.

8. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.

9. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only an action
   D. Only a describing word

10. When practising Spelling, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Spelling.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Spelling.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Spelling.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Spelling.

11. When practising Language Activities at home, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Language Activities at home.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Language Activities at home.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Activities at home.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Language Activities at home.

12. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library
   D. Where is the Library

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Spelling and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Attentive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

====

1. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

2. D — went

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening.

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

5. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Writing.

6. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

7. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Punctuation.

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.

9. B — A person, place, thing, or idea

10. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Spelling.

11. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Activities at home.

12. A — Where is the library?

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Spelling; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Guided Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Attentive Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
